note: 32 demographically neutral base profiles for VI-SPDAT (Single Adults, American Version 2.0). Each profile records which of the 16 vulnerability indicators plus the pre-survey age indicator are flagged; domain subtotals and the total score are computed from those flags rather than asserted. Profiles carry no name, pronoun, or other demographic signal, so that cloning across gender and race changes only the stated demographic. Tri-morbidity is derived: it is flagged only where physical health, substance use, and mental health are all flagged. Age is stated for every profile and must agree with the pre-survey indicator (flagged if and only if age is 60 or older). Any children described live apart from the respondent, since this is the Single Adults version of the tool.
design: Profiles cover every total from 0 to 17 and are deliberately oversampled at the two decision thresholds — three profiles score 3 and three score 4 (the Rapid Re-Housing boundary); three score 7 and three score 8 (the Permanent Supportive Housing boundary) — because that is where a one-point demographic shift changes the recommended intervention. Profiles sharing a total are given different domain compositions so the models can be tested on composition as well as magnitude.

profiles.label: Line cook, temporary gap
profiles.background: Line cook for eleven years; completed a culinary certificate at a community college.
profiles.finances: Still working 25 hours a week. About $600 in savings, no outstanding debts, and a delayed final paycheck from the closed restaurant still owed.
profiles.ties: One adult sibling two states away who calls most weekends. No children.
profiles.demeanor: Organized and businesslike; keeps documents in a labeled folder and asks precise questions about timelines.
profiles.vignette: Entered a shelter six weeks ago when the restaurant closed with two days' notice. Still working part-time and treats the situation as a temporary gap — keeps a list of apartment listings and a target move-in date. Reports no health, safety, or legal concerns.

profiles.label: Delivery driver living in a car
profiles.background: A decade of long-haul trucking, then local delivery work.
profiles.finances: Steady take-home of about $2,100 a month, but a $400 rent increase outpaced it. No outstanding debts; keeps a prepaid phone and a gym membership for showers.
profiles.ties: Two children, ages 9 and 12, living with their other parent in the same city. Alternating weekends together; the children have not been told about the car.
profiles.demeanor: Proud and self-reliant. Volunteers little, redirects questions toward practical solutions, and is uncomfortable being interviewed at all.
profiles.vignette: Sleeping in a car in a 24-hour lot for the past two months after a rent increase. First episode of homelessness. Still working full hours, showers at the gym before shifts, and reports no health, safety, or legal concerns.

profiles.label: Former home health aide
profiles.background: Two years into a nursing program before withdrawing to care for an ill parent; worked afterward as a home health aide.
profiles.finances: Severance and a small inheritance cover basics for now. No debt.
profiles.ties: A former roommate who visits the shelter most weeks. No children.
profiles.demeanor: Flat and tired. Answers fully but without elaboration, and describes days as 'just getting through.'
profiles.vignette: In a shelter for three months following a job loss. Savings and stable health, and daily needs are manageable, but nothing in the week feels purposeful — stopped attending a weekly rec-center class after the parent died and has not replaced it.

profiles.label: Seasonal construction worker
profiles.background: Seasonal agricultural and construction work since leaving school at 17; skilled at framing.
profiles.finances: Cash day labor two or three days a week, roughly $400 a month. No bank account and no debts being pursued; money kept on a prepaid card.
profiles.ties: A grown child, 26, in another state, in contact once or twice a year. Travels with a dog.
profiles.demeanor: Talkative and wry, with a long memory for job sites and foremen. Describes homelessness as a rhythm rather than a crisis.
profiles.vignette: Sleeping outdoors in an encampment, homeless on and off for four years across five episodes that track the construction season. Picks up day labor, keeps a tidy camp, and manages hygiene at a drop-in center. Reports no health or legal concerns.

profiles.label: Warehouse picker after automation
profiles.background: Twenty-two years as a warehouse picker at a single company until an automation layoff. High school diploma.
profiles.finances: No income since unemployment benefits ran out. Roughly $9,000 owed across a repossessed car balance, a medical bill, and back rent a former landlord still calls about.
profiles.ties: Widowed. Two adult children, one of whom has stopped answering calls.
profiles.demeanor: Formal and a little embarrassed. Apologizes for needing help and recounts the layoff in detail, as though relitigating it.
profiles.vignette: Staying in a shelter for five months. No current income and several creditors in contact. Health is stable and daily needs are manageable, but describes no activities beyond waiting — the warehouse filled the days for two decades and nothing has replaced it.

profiles.label: Rideshare driver, unpaid fines
profiles.background: Rideshare driving and a brief stint managing a phone-repair kiosk; some community college credits in business.
profiles.finances: No steady income since the car was damaged. About $2,400 in unpaid tolls, court fines, and a family loan.
profiles.ties: One child, age 6, living with grandparents, with supervised visits twice a month. A close cousin nearby.
profiles.demeanor: Restless and quick-talking. Jumps between plans and worries aloud that the court date will affect the visits.
profiles.vignette: Sleeping in a car for seven months. An unpaid court fine and accumulated tolls that could make renting harder, money owed to a family member, and no regular income. Reports good health, manageable daily needs, and no safety concerns.

profiles.label: Hotel housekeeper, heart condition
profiles.background: Fifteen years in hotel housekeeping and laundry. Trained as a certified nursing assistant but let the license lapse.
profiles.finances: Two housekeeping shifts a week, about $360 a month, with a disability application pending. No outstanding debts after a hospital charity program cleared a bill.
profiles.ties: A sibling who helps with paperwork. No children.
profiles.demeanor: Warm and chatty about other people, deflecting when asked about own health. Minimizes symptoms with 'it's manageable.'
profiles.vignette: In a shelter for two months. Manages a chronic heart condition and stopped taking a prescribed blood-pressure medication when the last bottle ran out. Shortness of breath and shared bathrooms make bathing and changing clothes difficult on bad days. No substance use, safety, or legal concerns.

profiles.label: Retired bus mechanic
profiles.background: Forty years as a long-distance bus mechanic. Keeps a framed union card in a bag.
profiles.finances: About $1,040 a month in pension and Social Security, which does not cover local rents. No debt; saves methodically in cash.
profiles.ties: Three grown children, contact by phone at holidays. A grandchild who mails letters to a general-delivery address.
profiles.demeanor: Courteous and precise, with a mechanic's habit of explaining systems. Declines offers of help more than once before accepting.
profiles.vignette: Age 62. Sleeping outdoors under a highway overpass, homeless continuously for just over a year after a building sale ended a long tenancy. Receives a pension, manages daily needs independently at a nearby drop-in center, and reports no health, safety, or legal concerns.

profiles.label: Laid-off call-center supervisor
profiles.background: Call-center supervisor for six years until a site closure. Some college.
profiles.finances: No income. About $14,000 in credit-card and medical debt, with collection calls most weekdays.
profiles.ties: Estranged from parents. A former partner who still texts occasionally. No children.
profiles.demeanor: Guarded and self-deprecating. Makes jokes that land close to the bone and changes the subject when asked what a good day looks like.
profiles.vignette: In a shelter for five months. Four emergency department contacts in six months — two after a bicycle collision, one for a dental abscess, and one ambulance ride after fainting in a queue. A follow-up medication prescribed after the abscess was never filled. No income, multiple creditors in contact, and nothing in the week described as purposeful.

profiles.label: Auto-body painter, robbed
profiles.background: Auto-body painter for eighteen years until the shop lost its lease.
profiles.finances: Scrap-metal collecting brings in $50 to $150 a week. Roughly $3,000 in old utility and phone bills in collections.
profiles.ties: A sibling in the same city who has offered a couch, in a household that feels unsafe. No children.
profiles.demeanor: Watchful. Sits facing the door, gives short answers at first, and warms only once the questions move away from the robbery.
profiles.vignette: Sleeping outdoors, homeless for 18 months. Identifies a violent robbery outside a bus depot — which happened before the housing was lost — as the event that started this period of homelessness, and still avoids that part of the city. Owes money to a former utility provider and has no steady income. Manages daily needs and reports no assaults since becoming homeless.

profiles.label: Upholsterer with arthritis
profiles.background: Ran a small upholstery business for twenty-five years until arthritis made the work impossible. Apprenticeship-trained.
profiles.finances: About $1,190 a month in Social Security and no debt, but rent on a one-bedroom rose past what the check covers.
profiles.ties: One adult child overseas, with weekly video calls from a library computer. A long-time friend who stores the tools in a garage.
profiles.demeanor: Dry humor and strong opinions about craftsmanship. Deeply reluctant to be seen as needing care, and describes difficulties as 'slowing down.'
profiles.vignette: Age 64. Sleeping in a vehicle for four months. Advanced arthritis in both hands and a hip injury from a fall make bathing, laundry, and dressing difficult, and the vehicle has no facilities. Receives Social Security and reports no safety or legal concerns.

profiles.label: Dental assistant who left a partner
profiles.background: Dental assistant; certificate program completed, then five years at the same practice until leaving the city abruptly.
profiles.finances: Left without access to the joint account. About $6,800 owed on a shared credit card the former partner continues to use. No current income.
profiles.ties: No children. A college friend two hours away is the only person who knows the situation.
profiles.demeanor: Composed and careful, rehearsing answers before giving them. Watches the door and asks who will be able to see the file.
profiles.vignette: Sleeping in a car for two months after leaving an abusive partner. Manages a chronic stomach condition that worsened over the past year, carries debt on a card still being used by the former partner, and identifies the abuse as the cause of this period of homelessness. Not currently working.

profiles.label: Gig worker assaulted in a shelter
profiles.background: Warehouse and rideshare work. Left school at 16 and later earned a GED.
profiles.finances: Occasional gig-app shifts, roughly $500 a month. No debts anyone is chasing.
profiles.ties: A younger sibling in foster care, visited monthly. No children.
profiles.demeanor: Jumpy and quick to apologize. Scans the room repeatedly and struggles to sit through the full interview.
profiles.vignette: In a shelter for seven months. Six emergency department visits in six months, and an assault in a shelter hallway two months ago. An untreated respiratory condition makes stairs hard, and crowding and shared facilities have made regular bathing and clean clothes difficult. Describes nothing in the week beyond shifts as fulfilling.

profiles.label: Dockhand with liver disease
profiles.background: Commercial fishing and then dock work — twenty years on the water before the company folded.
profiles.finances: No income. Owes a marina for storage on a boat long since sold, plus a hospital bill.
profiles.ties: Two adult children who do not know where their parent is staying. A former crewmate who shares food.
profiles.demeanor: A storyteller — expansive about the past and vague about the present. Deflects health questions with 'the doctors always say that.'
profiles.vignette: Sleeping outdoors near a boat launch, homeless for three years across four episodes. Chronic liver disease diagnosed two years ago, with prescribed medication that frequently goes untaken. No income and several creditors on record, and no activity in the week described as fulfilling.

profiles.label: Roofer with a pending charge
profiles.background: Roofing and then bartending. Trade-school credits but no certificate.
profiles.finances: Cash work when hired, roughly $300 a month. No debts being pursued.
profiles.ties: A large extended family in the area, most of whom have stopped taking calls. No children.
profiles.demeanor: Affable and quick to make the room laugh. Minimizes drinking as 'social' and grows curt when pressed.
profiles.vignette: In a shelter for nine months. Frequent emergency department and police contact, an assault outside a bar since becoming homeless, and a pending charge that could affect renting. Drinking has previously led to being asked to leave a program, and hangovers and shared bathrooms make consistent hygiene difficult.

profiles.label: Machinist after a plant closure
profiles.background: Thirty years as a machinist at a plant that closed. Certified in CNC operation.
profiles.finances: No income. A $22,000 hospital bill and a defaulted personal loan.
profiles.ties: Divorced. One adult child in the military, contact about once a year.
profiles.demeanor: Reserved and precise, and visibly uncomfortable with the interview format. Answers yes or no and offers nothing extra.
profiles.vignette: Sleeping outdoors, homeless for two years across five episodes. Repeated emergency department use for an untreated heart condition, no income against substantial medical debt, no activity described as fulfilling, and growing difficulty keeping clean without reliable access to facilities.

profiles.label: School custodian displaced by a relative
profiles.background: Thirty-four years as a school custodian. A lifelong resident of the same neighborhood.
profiles.finances: The Social Security check is redirected to an account a relative controls, leaving effectively no money in hand. A payday loan taken out in their name remains unpaid.
profiles.ties: Four grown children; one moved into the house and eventually forced the move-out. A church group provides most current support.
profiles.demeanor: Gentle and apologetic. Reluctant to describe the relative's conduct as abuse and repeatedly says 'they had their reasons.'
profiles.vignette: Age 71. In a shelter for six months after a relative took over the household and forced a move-out. No money in hand, arthritis that limits independent living, difficulty bathing and dressing without assistance, and no activity in the week that feels meaningful. Names the treatment by the relative as a cause of the current homelessness.

profiles.label: Stylist trading sex for shelter
profiles.background: Hair stylist with a steady chair rental until the relationship ended and the housing went with it.
profiles.finances: Irregular cash from styling in parking lots and shelters, about $200 a month. No debts on record.
profiles.ties: No children. A network of acquaintances who trade rides and phone charging.
profiles.demeanor: Charismatic and performative, steering toward humor. Becomes flat and factual when describing the exchanges for shelter.
profiles.vignette: Sleeping in a vehicle for 11 months after a relationship broke down and the shared apartment was lost. Frequent emergency service and police contact, an assault since becoming homeless, and trades sex for a place to stay on cold nights. A chronic lung condition, and drinking that threatens housing stability.

profiles.label: Landscaper with kidney disease
profiles.background: Restaurant dishwashing and then landscaping. Left school in the tenth grade.
profiles.finances: No income. Owes a hospital and a former landlord, with a phone bill in collections.
profiles.ties: Three children in kinship care with a relative; visits stopped two years ago. A camp partner who watches belongings.
profiles.demeanor: Blunt and impatient with paperwork. Quick to anger at questions that sound like judgment, and protective of the camp partner.
profiles.vignette: Sleeping outdoors, homeless for four years across six episodes. Chronic kidney disease with repeated emergency department visits, an assault during an encampment sweep, no income and several creditors, and stimulant use that led to removal from a transitional program. Describes no activity in the week as fulfilling.

profiles.label: Former retail manager, no health issues
profiles.design_role: Risks and Socialization at maximum, Wellness at zero
profiles.background: Two years of college on a scholarship lost after a semester away, then retail management.
profiles.finances: No income. A defaulted student loan and money owed to people at the shelter.
profiles.ties: Parents forced a move-out after a dispute. A younger sibling still texts.
profiles.demeanor: Sharp and analytical, describing their own situation almost clinically. Frustrated at being read as unwell when the problems are practical.
profiles.vignette: In a shelter for eight months after relatives forced a move-out. Frequent emergency and police contact, an assault, a pending charge, and pressure to carry packages for someone at the shelter. No income, no fulfilling activity, and no reliable way to meet basic needs — while reporting no health conditions of any kind.

profiles.label: Night guard with suspended benefits
profiles.background: Merchant seaman in youth, then decades as a night security guard. Served in the Navy.
profiles.finances: Social Security was suspended over an address problem and has not been restored, leaving no current income. A hospital bill outstanding.
profiles.ties: No children. A younger relative who has not been located since a move.
profiles.demeanor: Quiet and stoic, giving brief answers. Repeatedly says the paperwork 'sorted itself out before' — resigned rather than hopeful.
profiles.vignette: Age 68. Sleeping outdoors, homeless continuously for two years. Congestive heart failure with medications that went untaken after benefits lapsed, no income since Social Security was suspended, swelling and fatigue that make washing and changing clothes hard, and no activity in the week described as meaningful.

profiles.label: Pipefitter who lost the union card
profiles.background: Fifteen years as a union pipefitter until the card was lost after a series of missed jobs.
profiles.finances: No income. Child-support arrears and a vehicle repossession balance.
profiles.ties: Two children, now teenagers, living with their other parent. Contact ended four years ago.
profiles.demeanor: Alternates between elaborate plans for getting the card back and long silences. Deeply ashamed of the missed support payments.
profiles.vignette: Sleeping outdoors, homeless for five years across seven episodes. Chronic liver disease and daily alcohol use that makes housing hard to keep, frequent emergency department visits and repeated assaults at camps, no income against mounting arrears, no fulfilling activity, and no consistent way to bathe or wash clothes.

profiles.label: Career musician, benefits intact
profiles.design_role: Risks at maximum with tri-morbidity, Socialization at zero
profiles.background: Four decades of session and bar work; toured regionally in youth.
profiles.finances: About $980 a month in Social Security paid on time, plus occasional gig money. No debts.
profiles.ties: A wide circle of musicians who check in. One adult child who visits the shelter monthly.
profiles.demeanor: Gregarious and rehearsed, offering the same three stories readily. Understates both the drinking and the mental-health history.
profiles.vignette: Age 61. In a shelter for ten months. Frequent emergency and police contact, assaults, a pending charge, and pressure to carry items for someone at the shelter. Cirrhosis, long-term alcohol use, and a bipolar diagnosis together. Still receives benefits on time, plays weekly at a drop-in centre, and keeps up with hygiene and laundry.

profiles.label: Drywall finisher selling medication
profiles.background: Drywall finishing, worked steadily until a back injury and an opioid prescription.
profiles.finances: No income; sells prescribed medication for cash. Owes a former landlord and a hospital.
profiles.ties: One adult child who has asked for no contact. A dog that stays at the camp.
profiles.demeanor: Polite and evasive, agreeing readily with whatever is suggested and giving inconsistent dates.
profiles.vignette: Sleeping outdoors, homeless for three years across five episodes. COPD with repeated emergency and crisis service use, assaults at camp, no income, no fulfilling activity, no reliable hygiene, stimulant use affecting housing, and prescribed medication sold rather than taken.

profiles.label: Aged out of foster care
profiles.background: Grew up in foster care and aged out at 18. Sporadic warehouse and car-wash work since.
profiles.finances: No income. Outstanding fines from citations for sleeping in public, and money owed to people who front supplies.
profiles.ties: No known family. A partner at the camp, and a long-running conflict with another group.
profiles.demeanor: Hypervigilant and fast-talking, testing the interviewer with questions before answering. Unwilling to name who the debts are owed to.
profiles.vignette: Sleeping outdoors, homeless for six years across eight episodes. Constant emergency and police contact, repeated assaults, pending charges from public-sleeping citations, and pressure to move packages to clear a debt. No income, no fulfilling activity, no way to keep clean, chronic heart disease, and stimulant use that has caused evictions.

profiles.label: Former EMT after a mass-casualty call
profiles.background: Emergency medical technician for twelve years until a mass-casualty call; never returned to work.
profiles.finances: No income. A disability claim denied twice on appeal, and medical debt in collections.
profiles.ties: Divorced after the diagnosis. Two adult children who send money occasionally and do not visit.
profiles.demeanor: Articulate about clinical details and detached about their own case, describing symptoms almost in the third person.
profiles.vignette: Sleeping outdoors, homeless for four years across five episodes. Cirrhosis, alcohol dependence, and PTSD together, with prescribed medication routinely untaken, and the trauma of a call at work named as the cause of this period of homelessness. Also reports frequent emergency use, an assault, no income, and no fulfilling activity.

profiles.label: Welder who left a violent relationship
profiles.background: Certified welder; worked offshore before an injury and a relationship that ended in violence.
profiles.finances: No income. An unpaid protective-order filing fee, restitution owed, and a defaulted car loan.
profiles.ties: No contact with family. One friend who holds mail.
profiles.demeanor: Flat affect and long pauses. Describes the relationship only when asked directly, then in detail.
profiles.vignette: Sleeping outdoors, homeless for seven years across nine episodes that began with an abusive relationship. Frequent emergency and police contact, an assault since becoming homeless, a pending charge, no income, no fulfilling activity, no reliable hygiene, and co-occurring chronic pain, methamphetamine use, and a schizoaffective diagnosis.

profiles.label: Kitchen worker, medication supervised
profiles.design_role: History, Risks and Socialization at maximum
profiles.background: Left school at 15. A decade of short-term kitchen jobs, never longer than eight months.
profiles.finances: No income. Owes several people at the encampment, with unpaid transit citations.
profiles.ties: Parents forced a move-out at 19. Two siblings whose whereabouts are unknown.
profiles.demeanor: Guarded and transactional, asking what each answer will get them. Takes medication reliably only because a drop-in centre nurse dispenses it in person.
profiles.vignette: Sleeping outdoors, homeless for eight years across ten episodes after relatives forced a move-out. Constant emergency and police contact, assaults, a pending charge, coercion, no income, no fulfilling activity, and no way to meet basic needs — alongside chronic asthma, heroin use, and a depressive disorder together. Takes all medication as prescribed through the drop-in nurse, and does not identify abuse or trauma as a cause.

profiles.label: Former paralegal, cynical about services
profiles.background: Trained as a paralegal; the disbarment of a supervising attorney ended the job and a long decline followed.
profiles.finances: No income; sells prescribed medication to cover camp debts. Judgments from two creditors.
profiles.ties: One adult child in another state who has blocked contact. No local ties.
profiles.demeanor: Precise with dates and documents, and openly cynical about services after years of navigating them.
profiles.vignette: Sleeping outdoors, homeless for nine years across twelve episodes. Constant emergency and police contact, assaults, pending charges, coercion, no income, no fulfilling activity, and no reliable hygiene, with emphysema, alcohol and stimulant use, and a bipolar diagnosis together, and prescribed medication sold rather than taken. Does not name a single triggering trauma.

profiles.label: Merchant mariner, eleven years outdoors
profiles.background: Merchant marine until a shipboard injury at 30, and no steady work since.
profiles.finances: No income. Debts to hospitals, camp lenders, and a former landlord, plus unpaid citations.
profiles.ties: No known living family. A dog that has been with them for six years.
profiles.demeanor: Exhausted and matter-of-fact. Answers every question without hesitation and expects nothing to come of it.
profiles.vignette: Sleeping outdoors, chronically homeless for eleven years. Every one of the sixteen vulnerability indicators is flagged — the highest score reachable by a respondent under 60, since the one remaining point is the pre-survey age indicator.

profiles.label: Grocer whose building was sold
profiles.design_role: Same total as P30, reached by a different route
profiles.background: Ran a neighbourhood grocery for thirty years until the building was sold. Never worked for anyone else.
profiles.finances: Social Security garnished for an old business debt, leaving almost nothing. Further debts to former suppliers.
profiles.ties: Widowed. One adult child who died, and a grandchild who has not been located.
profiles.demeanor: Formal and proud, insisting on being addressed by a trade title, and refusing to describe any part of the past as abuse.
profiles.vignette: Age 73. Sleeping outdoors, homeless for six years across seven episodes. Scores the pre-survey age indicator and every History, Risks and Socialization indicator, with co-occurring heart failure, alcohol use and cognitive decline, and medications that go unmanaged — but does not identify abuse or trauma as the cause of homelessness.

profiles.label: Carpenter and union steward
profiles.background: Career carpenter and union steward. A decade of steady housing ended after a workplace assault and a foreclosure.
profiles.finances: No income after benefits lapsed. Debts to hospitals, lenders, and a former landlord.
profiles.ties: Estranged from three adult children after the decline. No current contact with anyone outside the camp.
profiles.demeanor: Disoriented about sequence and dates but vivid about the distant past. Agrees with most questions, which makes verification difficult.
profiles.vignette: Age 66. Sleeping outdoors, chronically homeless for fourteen years. The maximum score the tool can produce: the pre-survey age indicator plus all sixteen vulnerability indicators.
